choices.reason: Ethyl acetoacetate at 20/1 was measured at 24.23/64.37 mL against a premeasurement prediction of 14.95/30.53; 10/1 tests how far that error extends down the solvent-ratio curve.
The methoxyethyl acetoacetate analogue was measured near 43.20/101.44 mL at 5/1; its 1/1 condition probes the steep lower-ratio part of the same chemical family.
A 1/1 measurement of the multifunctional acetoacetate ester tests whether the low-ratio behavior of simpler beta-keto esters transfers to this larger molecule.
Acetoxybenzaldehyde at 10/1 was measured at 43.63/75.43 mL, far above its premeasurement prediction. The 5/1 candidate tests the condition slope underlying that observed error.
Observed trifluoromethoxyphenol responses at 1/1 and 10/1 show ratio-dependent prediction errors; 50/1 tests whether that trend persists at the lean end.
Nitrobenzophenone has an irregular observed V2 sequence across 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1. A 1/1 point helps characterize the response curve without treating V2−V1 as uncertainty.
Methylquinoline at 10/1 tests transfer from the previously underpredicted quinoline and other measured aza-aromatics to a close new analogue.
Acetophenone oxime was measured at 43.11/119.20 mL at 50/1. The 20/1 candidate constrains its high-retention condition slope while the separate 10/1 CW selection remains unmeasured.
Ortho-fluorobenzonitrile was measured at 20.19/43.54 mL at 50/1, above its premeasurement prediction. A 10/1 point tests whether that discrepancy transfers across solvent ratios.
Ortho-tolunitrile at 10/1 adds a substituent contrast to the fluorobenzonitrile ratio probe, testing whether the nitrile response depends on the ortho group.
Salicylaldehyde has measured endpoints at 0/1 and 50/1, including a large V2 error at 0/1. The 20/1 candidate tests the interior of that curve.
Ortho-isopropylphenol at 50/1 probes whether the phenolic high-ratio behavior seen for salicylaldehyde and trifluoromethoxyphenol transfers to a less oxygenated analogue.
Fluorenone at 10/1 extends the measured aromatic-ketone series to a fused, conformationally constrained scaffold.
Bromobenzofuran at 50/1 tests a fused heteroaromatic scaffold with sparse direct feedback and adds a chemical contrast to the aromatic carbonyl probes.
The measured 50/1 ethyl fluorobenzoate and methyl iodobenzoate rows were overpredicted. This tert-butyl-substituted benzoate tests whether that ester-family error transfers.
Dibenzyl ether at 50/1 adds an ether-rich aromatic contrast to the ester and ketone selections, checking generalization beyond the measured carbonyl families.

hypotheses.statement: Beta-keto ester retention has a condition-dependent error that may transfer across ester substituents and molecular complexity.
The large observed acetoxybenzaldehyde error at 10/1 reflects a mislearned solvent-ratio response.
Trifluoromethoxyphenol prediction error changes substantially with PE/EA ratio.
Nitrobenzophenone's measured V2 response does not follow the model's smooth ratio trend.
The aza-aromatic underprediction transfers from quinoline to methylquinoline.
The oxime's large V2 at 50/1 persists into intermediate ratios.
Ortho-substituted benzonitrile errors depend on both solvent ratio and substituent identity.
Phenolic compounds share a high-ratio response pattern despite differing second functional groups.
Fused aromatic scaffolds expose transfer errors not resolved by the measured open-chain aromatic series.
Observed high-ratio benzoate overprediction may generalize to other lipophilic benzoates, while an ether contrast tests its chemical specificity.

feedback_interpretation: The latest acquired rows show especially large V2 underprediction for ethyl acetoacetate at 20/1 and large premeasurement errors for acetoxybenzaldehyde at 10/1, alongside ratio-dependent errors in phenols and aromatic carbonyls. The selection emphasizes condition curves and nearby chemical contrasts around those observed failures. Round-4 CW candidates have predictions but no revealed measurements; none is treated as observed feedback.
